title: Ankhorage Authentication
summary: Defines provider-neutral authentication ports and the authentication capability catalog for independent Ankhorage applications and adapters.
purpose: Provide stable authentication operations and boundary types so provider adapters can implement sign-in, sessions, password recovery, OTP, and OAuth without coupling consumers to a specific identity provider.
responsibilities: Publish the authentication capability catalog for sign-in, sign-up, sign-out, sessions, password recovery, OTP, and OAuth authorization.
Define the AuthPort boundary implemented by provider-specific authentication adapters.
Define host-supplied durable session and one-time authorization-attempt persistence ports.
Use portable authentication contracts from @ankhorage/contracts/auth at the public package boundary.
boundaries: Does not implement a concrete identity-provider SDK, session store, cryptography provider, or user directory.
Does not select, configure, or compose provider adapters for an application.
Does not own application-specific authorization policy or business workflows.
audience: Application and runtime authors that invoke provider-neutral authentication capabilities.
Maintainers of provider adapters that implement the AuthPort boundary.
useCases: Describe a sign-in or sign-up operation independently of the selected identity provider.
Invoke session, password-reset, OTP, or OAuth authorization flows through a common capability catalog.
Implement a provider adapter against the public AuthPort and published authentication contracts.

architecture.role: Provider-neutral authentication boundary library with an explicit port and capability catalog.
invariants: Concrete provider, persistence, and cryptography behavior remains behind host adapters rather than in this package.
Authentication inputs and results use published portable contracts.
Consumers depend on public package exports rather than provider-specific internals.

limitations: Applications must choose and configure a concrete provider adapter separately.
The package publishes persistence boundaries but does not persist sessions or credentials itself.
